 This Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 & 227 Of
The Constitution Of India, Praying To Declare That
The Respondents Have No Right Whatsoever Over The
Petition Schedule Property Comprised In Sy.No.341 Of
Banaswadi Village, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bangalore East
Taluk (Formerly Bangalore South Taluk) Measuring 2
Acres And 26 Guntas In Extent In Lieu Of
De-Notification Issued By The First Respondent As Per
Gazette Notification Vide Annexure-A, Etc.
 This Petition Coming On For Orders, Through
Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing This Day, The
Court Made The Following:
 -3-
 Nc: 2024:Khc:2068
 Wp No. 44712 of 2014
 Order
1.

Respondent no.2/Bangalore Development Authority ('Bda' for short) has acquired certain lands
in Survey No.341 of Banaswadi village, K.R.Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk.

However, certain
lands in
Survey No.341 were later de-notified.
The case of the petitioner is that his land falls within the de-notified area.
The same is disputed by respondent no.2/BDA.
However, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the BDA that truth can be ascertained after proper survey of the area.

It is T Munirathnam vs The State Of Karnataka on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138926467/
2 further submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that in the process of completing the acquisition proceedings, respondent no.2/BDA has illegally demolished a portion of the building of the petitioner and he is entitled to claim compensation for the same and has prayed that a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- should be awarded to him as compensation.
2.

sentences.text: Admittedly, a survey requires to be conducted for ascertaining whether the land belonging to the petitioner falls within the de-notified area or the area which has been acquired by the BDA.
The learned counsel for the BDA NC: 2024:KHC:2068 further submits that necessary survey will be conducted within two months by issuing notice to the petitioner to be present at the time of survey.
The same is acceptable to the petitioner.

3. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation for demolished portion of his building or not can be decided only upon completion of the survey and the petitioner would be entitled to it only if it is found that his property falls in the de-notified area and not the area acquired by the BDA.

Further,
the petitioner will have to prove the actual damages suffered by him to claim any compensation.

4. Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Respondent nos.2 and 3 are directed to conduct survey of the land of the petitioner after due notice to him and determine whether the said land is acquired for the purposes of BDA or not, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

(ii) If it is found that the land of the petitioner falls in the de-notified area or in the area which is not NC: 2024:KHC:2068 acquired by the BDA and that the petitioner's construction has been illegally demolished by the BDA, the petitioner will have a right to approach the Civil Court to claim compensation and will have the benefit of Section 14 of the Limitation Act for filing such a suit, if he is so advised.
( iii )

Till a decision is taken by the BDA by conducting the necessary survey,
respondent nos.2 and 3 shall maintain status quo in respect of the property concerned.
(iv) The writ petition stands disposed of accordingly.

Sd/-
JUDGE hkh.
